parallel_fusion.note: Main now explicitly requires loader-consumed-byte/physical-engine-lease evidence because pre-load hashing is not loader attestation. This receipt hardens the earlier pre-load directory digest itself against membership changes during hashing; it does not claim to solve loader attestation.

finding.before_behavior: digest_artifact_path enumerated directory members once, then hashed that frozen member list. A file added after enumeration was absent from the digest even though it existed before the function returned.
finding.risk_scope: A positive pre-load EngineAdmission could describe a tree that had already changed during hashing. This is source/control-plane integrity debt only; it is not evidence of a real model-loader exploit.

unusual_experiment.method: deterministically inject a new regular artifact member after the initial os.walk member enumeration and before the first listed member is hashed

source_delta.mechanism: enumerate regular tree membership through one helper before hashing, re-enumerate before return, and fail closed if relative member identity differs

limits: The member-set recheck does not make a writable artifact tree immutable after digest_artifact_path returns.
It does not prove that the model loader later consumes the admitted bytes.
A generation-fenced physical engine lease or enforced read-only/content-addressed loader boundary plus downstream consumed-byte echo remains required for HCU runtime credit.
No real ~0.8B model checkpoint/tokenizer/runtime was loaded by this cycle.
No whole EntityOS/HCU runtime acceptance is claimed.
next_gate: Retain this pre-load tree-membership fence while current main's loader-consumed-byte requirement is fused into the same HCU path; then run the exact retained engine-admission tests with the real router plus loader-lease/inference-echo integration in an actually-started authorized isolated executor before any runtime promotion.
